title: Testing Kotlin with kotlin.test
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of testing kotlin with kotlin.test using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates testing kotlin with kotlin.test.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Testing Kotlin with kotlin.test** as part of **Testing, Debugging, Documentation, and Quality**. Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Use the subtopics—Test Annotations and Assertions, Testing Common Kotlin Code, Integrating with Platform Test Frameworks—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

items.title: Test Annotations and Assertions
items.text: Test Annotations and Assertions helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Testing Kotlin with kotlin.test removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
